verificationLog.notes: openrouter-free joined tierAllowedModels.economy on 2026-09-06 (d02aed0b5), which puts it in the picker on every plan, but auto.tierAllowedSlots only carried its two slots, free_workhorse and free_workhorse_fast, under the free tier, so tierAdmissionRejection in packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts refused every explicit pick on Pro, Max, Enterprise and BYOK with "routing slot free_workhorse, free_workhorse_fast for model openrouter-free is not allowed for tier <tier>", reproduced live from the Chrome extension on an Enterprise account on 2026-09-14. The direct fix (adding those two slots to the paid tiers' lists) was tried and reverted: packages/ai/model-registry/tests/registry-contract.test.mjs asserts every non-free tier's allowed slots contain nothing prefixed free_, an invariant authored in 90ac37cc7 specifically so a paid tier could never reach a pool-gated model, and docs/research/free-inference-tos-workbook-2026-09-01.md independently excluded openrouter-free from the free lane's pool because OpenRouter's data_collection parameter defaults to allow (upstream training permitted) unless a caller sends deny. That invariant governs the automatic free lane (free-pools.json, free-auto.ts, FreeEligibility), a silent, system-initiated route the 2026-09-01 workbook is right to gate tightly; it was never a statement that openrouter-free itself may not be explicitly selected. The 2026-09-06 catalog entry for that change already drew exactly this line, made with the training-data fact in view: "those upstream providers' terms may allow training on prompts, which is why the company free lane... still lists no OpenRouter free route; the picker entry is a user choice, not the free lane." This change completes that already-made decision rather than revisiting it: a new tier-neutral slot, router_zero_cost, same modelKey openrouter-free, added after free_workhorse_fast in auto.slots (so free_workhorse stays the first-registered, canonical slot for this modelKey and getSlotForModel('openrouter-free') is unchanged) and appended to tierAllowedSlots for free, pro, max, enterprise and byok. It is deliberately absent from every task's preferredSlots, so policyReachableSlots in packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts never contains it and the Auto router can never place it in a fallback or task-ranked candidate list on any tier; it is reachable only by a caller naming openrouter-free directly, exactly like free_workhorse today. registry-contract.test.mjs gained one assertion enforcing that reachability stays absent, and its free-lane-slot invariant is otherwise untouched and still passes. The conformance fixture changed on exactly the three openrouter-free rows (two explicit selections, one continuity case, all previously unavailable at tier max) and is byte-identical to what the direct, reverted fix would have produced, which is expected: the two approaches are behaviourally equivalent for admission and differ only in whether a pool-only-by-naming-convention slot got reused, which is what the guard exists to prevent. Not addressed here, and out of this change's scope: whether the dispatch itself should force data_collection: deny for an explicit pick regardless of the caller's organization zeroDataRetentionOnly setting (packages/ai/providers/openrouter/src/provider-routing.ts only sends deny when that org-level flag is already true, which is opt-in and off by default). That is a request-dispatch change, not a routing-admission one, and a separate in-progress note in audit/decisions/founder-actions.md is already tracking it as a founder decision.

One current model per family. Audited all 26 family slots in model-families.json for a released same-family successor already in the catalog and found five families carrying two generations. qwen/qwen-flash was the only slot whose active model was the older one, so it is the only promotion: Qwen3.5-Flash to Qwen3.8-Flash. The other four already served the successor, so their predecessors were retired without a slot move: gemini-3.6-flash under gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.1-flash-lite under gemini-3.5-flash-lite, kimi-k2.6 under kimi-k3, and minimax-m2.7 under minimax-m3. minimax-m2.7 was also the last explicit model id left in tierAllowedModels.pro_additions beside minimax-m3 and it is gone from that list; every other tier entry is already a family slot reference, so those follow the promotion on their own. All five predecessors are deprecated rather than removed: the records stay in the catalog and stay resolvable, so a conversation that named one still opens, and lifecycle.deprecated takes them out of the picker and out of every routing target the compiler resolves. Evidence for the promotion. Qwen3.8-Flash answers: probed 2026-09-06 through its own default route, qwen/qwen-3.8-flash on the dashscope-intl endpoint, first byte at 1011 ms, echoing the model id qwen3.8-flash back, recorded in probes.json. The managed OpenRouter route was probed first because that is what managed cloud dispatches on for Qwen, and it returned 404 with every endpoint excluded by the account zero-data-retention setting at openrouter.ai/settings/privacy. That is an account policy rather than a model fact: the outgoing Qwen3.5-Flash fails the same way through the same route, while gemini-3.8-flash, kimi-k3 and minimax-m3 all answer through it. Release date and shape: models.dev publishes alibaba/qwen3.8-flash with release_date 2026-08-26, a 1,000,000-token context, 131,072 output tokens and 0.15 in / 0.47 out per million, and alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen3-8-flash, retrieved 2026-09-06 and last updated there 2026-08-28, confirms the same 1M context and 131,072 output ceiling. Neither source publishes benchmark scores for this model, so the advance from probed to evaluated rests on that published capability, limit and pricing record plus the live probe, not on comparative scores; that gap is stated here rather than papered over. Two judgments a reviewer should see. The promotion breached the default 25 percent input cost regression ceiling: input rises 0.10 to 0.15 per million, a 50 percent increase, while output rises 0.40 to 0.47, 17.5 percent, and context holds at 1M while max output more than doubles from 64,000 to 131,072. The per-family thresholds override that families.mjs already merges is set on qwen/qwen-flash at maxInputCostIncreaseRatio 0.5 so the slot accepts this generation, and it is recorded here because the family record has no field to carry a reason. Second, loadFamilySnapshot in scripts/compile.mjs never passed the gateway catalog to buildNormalizedRegistry, so every family slot command has crashed since gateways were introduced; the missing argument is restored, which is what made this audit possible at all.

Added the two OpenRouter router routes the product had no entry for: openrouter/auto (Auto Router) and openrouter/free (Free Models Router), and set open_router.defaultModel to openrouter/auto, which was previously empty so the provider had no route at all. Every field is read from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models retrieved 2026-08-29 with a live key. Auto Router: canonical_slug openrouter/auto, 2,000,000 context, tokenizer "Router", modality text+image+file+audio+video->text+image, and supported_parameters including reasoning, reasoning_effort, tools, tool_choice and structured_outputs, hence reasoning.control "effort". Free Models Router: canonical_slug openrouter/free, 200,000 context, modality text+image->text, pricing prompt "0" and completion "0", and supported_parameters including reasoning_effort, tools and structured_outputs. Both routes report pricing that is resolved per request, auto returns "-1" for prompt and completion because cost follows the model it selects, so no per-million rate is recorded here and reservation must price the resolved route, not the router. No benchmarks are recorded because OpenRouter publishes none for either router, and carrying a member model's numbers forward would be fabricated. openrouter/auto is recorded with inputCost/outputCost 0 because ModelMetadata requires both and the router publishes no rate of its own; managed metering must price the model the router actually resolved (the completion response reports it) rather than the router record, so this route is safe on BYOK, where OpenRouter bills the key holder directly, and must not be exposed on a metered managed plan until resolved-route pricing is wired. openrouter/free is genuinely zero-rated ("0"/"0" from the provider).

Both router routes were exercised end to end against the live API after the account key was rotated. openrouter/auto returned HTTP 200 in 752ms and reported routing to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, confirming the earlier note that the router itself publishes no rate and that metering must price the resolved model. openrouter/free returned HTTP 200 and routed to free members (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, minimax/minimax-m2.7:free) with usage.cost 0, confirming the zero rating. Both free members are reasoning models whose reasoning tokens count against max_tokens: a 16-token cap returned empty content while a 200-token cap returned the expected text with finish_reason "stop" and 31 reasoning tokens. The product default is DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8192, so this is not reachable in normal use, but any caller that lowers the cap for a free-router turn must leave room for reasoning tokens.

grok-4.7.name: Grok 4.7
grok-4.7.pricingNote: Base rate below 200,000 prompt tokens is $2.00/1M input, $6.00/1M output, $0.50/1M cached input. A request whose prompt reaches 200,000 tokens is billed at $4.00/$12.00/$1.00 for every token in the request. xAI publishes no cache-write price, so none is recorded. The batch API does not serve this model. Server-side tool calls are billed separately per invocation and the schema has no field for them. xAI states the model has no text output limit, so no maximum output length is recorded. xAI gives the release month only; the OpenRouter slug dates it 2026-09-16 and the Vercel AI Gateway list 2026-09-21, so the row records September 2026. Verified against docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.7, the models overview, the reasoning guide and the release notes, retrieved 2026-10-07.

veo-3.1.name: Veo 3.1
veo-3.1.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Standard with audio: $0.40/second at 720p or 1080p; $0.60/second at 4k. 1080p and 4k require 8-second generations.

veo-3.1-fast.name: Veo 3.1 Fast
veo-3.1-fast.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Fast with audio: $0.10/second at 720p, $0.12/second at 1080p, $0.30/second at 4k. 1080p and 4k require 8-second generations. Verified against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing on 2026-08-12.

gpt-4o-transcribe.name: GPT-4o Transcribe
gpt-4o-transcribe.pricingNote: $2.50/1M input, $10/1M output tokens; 16k context. Added to the Audio API on 2025-03-20. Shut down 2027-02-26 in favour of gpt-transcribe for file transcription and gpt-live-transcribe for realtime. File streaming with stream=true is supported and the model is served on /v1/realtime. Verified 2026-09-04.

gpt-live-1.name: GPT Live 1
gpt-live-1.pricingNote: Priced per minute of session rather than per token: sessionPerMinuteCost is the published $0.05 per minute of voice session, billed per second, so the per-token fields on this entry are zero rather than a rate. The delegated backend model and any tool usage are billed separately. Only v1/live/sessions serves this model and it is not offered on OpenRouter. Audio and text in, audio out with the transcript delivered as session events, with streaming and function calling; image and video are unsupported. Default voice marin. Knowledge cutoff 2025-07-31. Verified against https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1 and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live on 2026-09-10.

gpt-4o-mini-transcribe.name: GPT-4o Mini Transcribe
gpt-4o-mini-transcribe.pricingNote: $1.25/1M input, $5/1M output tokens; 16k context. Added to the Audio API on 2025-03-20; default snapshot gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15. Shut down 2027-02-26 in favour of gpt-transcribe for file transcription and gpt-live-transcribe for realtime; the 2025-03-20 snapshot shuts down earlier, on 2027-01-20. File streaming with stream=true is supported and the model is served on /v1/realtime. Verified 2026-09-04.

minimax-m3.name: MiniMax M3
minimax-m3.pricingNote: Standard tier, permanent 50% discount: $0.30/1M input and $1.20/1M output at or below 512K input tokens, rising to $0.60/$2.40 above 512K. Cache reads are $0.06/1M at the base band and $0.12/1M above 512K. M3 is served by passive caching on the OpenAI-compatible route the product calls, and MiniMax publishes no cache-write fee for it. Verified against platform.minimax.io, retrieved 2026-09-04.

veo-3.1-lite.name: Veo 3.1 Lite
veo-3.1-lite.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Lite with audio: $0.05/second at 720p, $0.08/second at 1080p. 4k output is NOT supported on Lite. Paid tier only. Verified end to end against veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview on 2026-08-06 (200 + completed operation).

gemini-omni-1.1-flash.name: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash
gemini-omni-1.1-flash.pricingNote: Paid tier only. Input $1.50/1M (text, image, video, audio); output $9.00/1M text and $17.50/1M video, which Google states is approximately $0.10 per second. Video output runs 3 to 10 seconds at 360p, 720p, 1080p or 4K and 24 frames per second. Google names this model as the replacement for gemini-omni-flash-preview and for the three Veo 3.1 ids, all of which shut down on 2026-10-22. Verified against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, the deprecations page and the model page, retrieved 2026-10-07.

gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.name: Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.pricingNote: Low-latency real-time speech-to-speech translation, 70+ languages. Free tier is free of charge; paid tier $3.50/1M input and $21.00/1M output audio tokens, equivalently $0.0053/min in and $0.0315/min out. Audio bills at 25 tokens per second, an effective ~$0.0368 per minute. Sourced from the published Gemini API pricing table, 2026-08-06. INTERIM: adopted while OpenAI's live/realtime API is unreleased; revisit when that ships.

gemini-3.8-live.name: Gemini 3.8 Live
gemini-3.8-live.pricingNote: Live API audio-to-audio dialogue model, served only over a live session. It can also return text there, but outputModalities lists audio alone, as the other live voice row does, so the chat path never routes a text request to it. Input $0.75/1M text, $3.00/1M audio (about $0.005 per minute) and $1.00/1M image or video (about $0.002 per minute). Output $4.50/1M text and $12.00/1M audio (about $0.018 per minute). Token limits are 131,072 in and 65,536 out. The model reasons between turns but takes no thinking level: Google says to omit thinking_level when moving from the 3.1 preview. Asynchronous function calling is the default, proactive audio is always on and affective dialogue is gone. Structured outputs, caching, batch and code execution are not supported. Google names this model as the replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, which shuts down on 2026-11-17. Verified against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, the deprecations page and the model page, retrieved 2026-10-07.

gemini-3.8-flash-tts.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
gemini-3.8-flash-tts.pricingNote: Google lists an introductory $0.50/1M text input and $9.00/1M audio output (about $0.00225 per 10 seconds of audio) through 2026-12-31. From 2027-01-01 the published rates are $1.00 and $18.00, carried in post_promo_prices. Batch and Flex are half; cached input is $0.125 rising to $0.25. Token limits are 8,192 in and 16,384 out. Returns WAV audio by default and covers over 130 languages. Google names this model, with gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts, as the replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview, which shuts down on 2026-11-17. Verified against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, the deprecations page and the model page, retrieved 2026-10-07.

openrouter-auto.name: OpenRouter Auto
openrouter-auto.pricingNote: OpenRouter publishes prompt and completion prices of -1 for the Auto Router, meaning the request is billed at the standard rate of whichever model the router selects, with no router fee. The zero rates carried here are a placeholder for that dynamic price, not a free route: meter managed traffic against the model named in the response, never at zero. Verified against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, retrieved 2026-09-04.

openrouter-auto-beta.name: OpenRouter Auto (Beta)
openrouter-auto-beta.pricingNote: Task-aware sibling of the Auto Router, still labelled Beta by OpenRouter, so it does not replace openrouter/auto. OpenRouter publishes prompt and completion prices of -1, meaning the request bills at the selected model's standard rate with no router fee; the zero rates here are a placeholder for that dynamic price, so meter the model named in the response and never at zero. No maximum completion length is published, so none is recorded. Verified against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, retrieved 2026-09-04.

gpt-oss-safeguard-20b.name: GPT-OSS Safeguard 20B
gpt-oss-safeguard-20b.pricingNote: Groq classes this as a preview model and warns that preview models are for evaluation only and may be discontinued at short notice, so the row is not selectable. Flat rate identical to gpt-oss-20b: $0.075/1M input, $0.30/1M output, $0.0375/1M cached input, which is the 50% cached-input discount Groq states applied to the input rate. Not on the batch eligibility list. This is a policy-following safety classifier that takes its own policy as input, Groq's replacement for Llama Guard 4, not a chat model. Verified against console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, retrieved 2026-09-04.

qwen-3.8-27b.name: Qwen3.8 27B
qwen-3.8-27b.pricingNote: Groq classes this as a preview model and warns that preview models are for evaluation only and may be discontinued at short notice, so the row is not selectable. Flat rate on Groq: $0.80/1M input, $4.00/1M output. Absent from both the prompt-caching and batch pages, so no cached rate and no batch discount apply. Adds strict JSON schema and five-level reasoning_effort over qwen3.6-27b. Thinking is turned off with reasoning_effort none. Groq prints the context window as 131,042 in both its models table and the model card, where every other Groq model reads 131,072; the documented figure is carried here as the safe lower bound. Groq publishes no knowledge cutoff. Verified against console.groq.com/docs/model/qwen/qwen3.8-27b, retrieved 2026-09-04.
